about.title: Paramount Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a loved one changes everything, and for families in Paramount, that loss often follows a crash on corridors like Garfield Avenue or Downey Avenue, where traffic volume peaks on Friday afternoons. Los Angeles County recorded 4 traffic deaths locally in the most recent final year, a reminder that even one loss ripples through an entire household. California law recognizes that spouses, domestic partners, and children carry the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible when no immediate family survives. These claims are separate from any criminal proceeding and exist to address the financial and emotional toll left behind: funeral costs, lost income the family relied on, and the loss of companionship and guidance a loved one provided. We handle wrongful death matters and can walk you through your options, without pressure and without a fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Act

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. We can help clarify who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim in California, though claims against a government entity involve a much shorter window. Waiting can quietly close doors, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Funeral Bill
items.desc: California law allows families to seek recovery for lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance, not just burial costs. We can help you understand what your family may be entitled to pursue.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. We can review your family's specific circumstances to confirm who has standing.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the other driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focused on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action focused on the family's losses. One can move forward independent of the other, and outcomes in one don't determine the other.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a busy Paramount street like Rosecrans or Alondra?
items.answer: The specific road doesn't change the legal standing to file, but details about how and where a crash happened can matter for building the case. Our team is familiar with local traffic patterns, including corridors that see higher volume on Friday afternoons, and can factor that into the review.

items.question: How much does it cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We offer a free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover something for your family.
